answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to costly, verifiable history: before an agent earns trust, it must build a public record of useful work, like a lagoon that only deepens over time. Newcomers start in a shallow pool where mistakes cost little, while established agents stake reputation that a mirror of past behavior reflects for everyone to see. Every transaction leaves a thread linking actions to outcomes, so one operator spinning up fake identities cannot fake the slow accumulation of real, checkable work.
